title: Hostinger or GoDaddy: which web host is worth it once you count the renewal?
seoTitle: Hostinger or GoDaddy: which costs less with renewal?
description: In US dollars, Hostinger Premium with SONAR20 costs less than GoDaddy Economy in the 1-, 2- and 4-year hosting comparisons. Domain and email renewals cost extra.
metaDescription: SONAR20 takes 20% off new 12-, 24- and 48-month Hostinger Premium purchases. Compare hosting and renewal costs with GoDaddy.
imageAlt: The Hostinger logo, a calendar and a renewal icon, with the title Hostinger vs GoDaddy on the band

contentSections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: In US dollars, Hostinger Premium with SONAR20 costs less than GoDaddy Economy over one, two and four years of hosting. Its quoted annual hosting renewal is also lower. Both include a domain and email free for the first year, and those renewals are not in the hosting totals.

contentSections.heading: The pair to compare
paragraphs: On Hostinger's international site, shared hosting starts at Premium, which includes a domain and email free for the first year. GoDaddy's plan with the same two items is Economy. These two are the main pair of this article. Both include a free SSL certificate on the plans compared here.

The article answers by horizon: what you pay in the first year, over 2 years and over 4 years, and what each plan charges to renew. GoDaddy also sells Starter, a plan with the site only, and it gets its own section further down.
Prices from the international sites and their carts, November 6, 2026.

rows: 2 mailboxes per site, free for 1 year

contentSections.heading: In the first year, Hostinger costs less
paragraphs: For a site that will last one year, Hostinger's 12-month Premium with SONAR20 costs US$19.10. GoDaddy Economy costs US$83.88 for its first year. The difference is US$64.78 in Hostinger's favor.

comparisonTable.caption: Twelve-month hosting prices recorded in the carts. Hostinger's price includes SONAR20. Check the full cart total for any separate charges.

postParagraphs: Hostinger's cart had the Black Friday price already applied: the 12-month Premium showed US$1.99 a month without the code and US$1.59 a month with SONAR20, the same monthly rate as the 24- and 48-month plans. The code gives 20% off a new purchase.

contentSections.heading: Over 2 years, Hostinger costs less
paragraphs: For two years of hosting, Premium's 24-month price with SONAR20 was US$38.21 upfront. Economy's 24-month price was US$155.76. At the quoted renewal rate, buying one year of Economy and renewing once would total US$227.76. One year of Starter plus one renewal at its quoted rate would total US$143.76.

comparisonTable.caption: Premium and Economy use their quoted 24-month upfront prices; Premium includes SONAR20. Starter uses one year plus one renewal at the quoted rate. Domain and email renewals after year one are excluded.
rows: GoDaddy Starter, 2 years (12 months plus 1 renewal at the same price)

contentSections.heading: Over 4 years, Hostinger costs less
paragraphs: Hostinger's 48-month purchase covers hosting for four years without a hosting renewal during that period. In the cart, the Black Friday price for Premium was US$95.52, reduced to US$76.42 with SONAR20. Domain and email renewals after the first year are separate.
For exactly four years of Economy hosting, the projection uses 36 months at US$215.64 plus one annual renewal at the quoted US$143.88. It totals US$359.52 if the renewal rate stays unchanged.

rows: US$215.64 for 36 months, plus 1 renewal of US$143.88
comparisonTable.caption: Premium uses a 48-month upfront purchase. Economy uses 36 months plus one annual renewal at the quoted rate.

postParagraphs: The quoted 60-month Economy price was US$359.40 upfront: US$0.12 less than the projected four-year route above, with a fifth year of hosting included. It is the lower total outlay of these two options, although it requires paying the full amount at the start.
The totals do not include renewing the domain or the email after the first year, at either company.

contentSections.heading: After the paid period: what each plan charges to renew
paragraphs: After the promotional term, Premium and Economy renew at their list prices. SONAR20 applies only to a new purchase. The cart quoted Premium's renewal after 48 months at US$131.88 for 12 months, equivalent to US$10.99 a month. It quoted the same renewal rate for the 12-month plan. Future renewal prices may change.
For Economy's one-year purchase, GoDaddy's cart quoted the next annual hosting renewal at US$143.88, US$12 more than Premium's quoted annual renewal.

contentSections.heading: What about the 1-month plan?
paragraphs: The cart quoted Premium at US$12.99 for one month, with the same monthly renewal price. SONAR20 did not reduce that price. At an unchanged rate, twelve monthly payments total US$155.88, about eight times the 12-month purchase with the code. Paying monthly can suit a short project or test, but costs more if you keep the site for a year.

contentSections.heading: If you only need the site: GoDaddy Starter
paragraphs: Starter is GoDaddy's plan with the site only: 1 site, 10 GB NVMe and cPanel, with no domain or email on the list. SSL comes through AutoSSL, like every GoDaddy plan. It has no first-year discount: the cart showed US$71.88 for 1 year, and it renews at the same US$71.88.

Starter costs more than Premium with SONAR20 in the one-, two- and four-year hosting comparisons. It has the lowest quoted annual renewal of the three plans, US$60 below Premium. That lower renewal does not make it cheaper overall within the first four years.

contentSections.heading: Domain, email and SSL: what expires after the first year
paragraphs: On Premium and Economy, the domain and email are free for one year. After that, each service renews separately at both companies. The two- and four-year hosting totals exclude those renewals. GoDaddy's notice also lists an ICANN fee for the free domain, so check the full cart total before paying.

Hostinger includes a free certificate, and GoDaddy includes AutoSSL, on the hosting plans compared here. The Economy cart also listed a Standard SSL, free for one year and then set to auto-renew at US$119.99 a year. That is an extra paid certificate on top of AutoSSL; check its renewal setting if you do not want to keep it.

contentSections.heading: Refunds: check GoDaddy's window for your plan
paragraphs: Hostinger accepts a refund request within 30 days of purchase. GoDaddy's international page lists 30 days on the plan cards; its footer gives a full refund within 30 days on an annual plan and within 48 hours on a monthly plan. Check the refund terms for the plan you buy, especially if it is monthly.

contentSections.heading: If you need more: Unlimited and Cloud Startup
paragraphs: Above Premium, Hostinger's page lists Unlimited, with unlimited sites, and Cloud Startup. At 20% off the page prices, the 48-month totals with SONAR20 are US$107.14 for Unlimited and US$306.82 for Cloud Startup, with advertised renewals of US$16.99 and US$25.99 a month. Those two totals are calculations; confirm them in the cart.

contentSections.heading: Which to choose, by how long the site will stay online
paragraphs: One year, with a domain and email: Hostinger Premium for 12 months with SONAR20, at US$19.10. Economy costs US$64.78 more in the same period.

Two years of hosting: Hostinger Premium for 24 months with SONAR20 costs US$38.21, against US$155.76 for Economy. Both include a domain and email free for the first year; add their separate renewal costs if you keep those services in year two.

Four years of hosting: Premium's 48-month price with SONAR20 was US$76.42. Economy projects to US$359.52 for 36 months plus one annual renewal at the quoted rate. Its 60-month offer was slightly lower, at US$359.40 upfront, but both options cost more than four times Premium's four-year price. Domain and email renewals are extra.

If you only need the site, Starter has the lowest annual renewal: US$71.88, against US$131.88 for Premium. Premium with SONAR20 still costs less over the first four years. For a longer project, compare accumulated payments over your intended term, using the renewal prices available when you buy.
In every case, check the renewal price in the cart before paying: promotions change.

contentSections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: Which is better, Hostinger or GoDaddy? For hosting costs, Premium with SONAR20 costs less than Economy over one, two and four years, and its annual renewal is lower. Domain and email renewals are extra. GoDaddy Starter has the lowest annual renewal, but costs more than Premium over the first four years. More criteria are in [how to choose a web host](/en/reviews/how-to-choose-web-host-hostinger).
Does GoDaddy renew at the same price? Economy does not: the cart shows the 1-year plan going from US$83.88 to US$143.88 at renewal. Starter has no first-year discount and renews at the same US$71.88.

Does the Hostinger coupon work on the renewal? No. SONAR20 applies to a new purchase only, and the renewal is charged at the list price. For the renewal, see the [Hostinger renewal guide](/en/reviews/hostinger-renewal-price-coupon-sonar20).
Does Hostinger Premium come with a domain? Yes, a domain and 2 mailboxes per site are free for the first year. After that, each renews separately.

Can I move my site from GoDaddy to Hostinger? Hostinger's help page says free migration covers a site from another company on the Web, Cloud or Agency plans. Check your plan with support before cancelling the old one.

What is the Hostinger coupon code? SONAR20 gives 20% off a new purchase of the 12-, 24- and 48-month Premium plans compared here; it does not apply to renewal and did not reduce the quoted one-month Premium price.

contentSections.heading: Who writes this
paragraphs: Em Casa com Cecília runs on Hostinger, and its domain is registered there. For GoDaddy, this text uses only what its international page and cart show in US dollars; no one on the team has used the service.

takeIf: Choose Hostinger Premium if you can pay upfront for 24 or 48 months of hosting: with SONAR20 it costs less than Economy in those comparisons, and the domain and email renewals are extra.
Choose Hostinger Premium if the project needs one year of hosting with a domain and email included: its 12-month price is lower than Economy's. Its quoted annual hosting renewal is also lower.
skipIf: Consider GoDaddy Starter if you only need hosting and prioritize the lowest quoted annual renewal. It costs more than Premium over the first four years; a longer-term choice needs a total-cost comparison for your intended duration.
Go with GoDaddy Economy if you prefer cPanel and accept paying more than Premium in the first year, over 2 and 4 years and at renewal.
